requirements.title: Outline data model and signature sanitising
requirements.rationale: Every consumer must receive the same shaped, sorted and sanitised declarations regardless of which backend produced them.

criteria.action: for any File it returns, set Backend to one of "go/ast", "ctags", "heuristic" or "none", and return Decls as a non-nil slice sorted by StartLine with ties broken by Name
criteria.contract: Backend is one of go/ast, ctags, heuristic, none; Decls is non-nil even when empty; for every adjacent pair, StartLine is non-decreasing and equal StartLines are ordered by Name

setup: a generator of sources across Go, heuristic languages, ctags-table-only languages and unknown extensions
a fake Runner that returns tags in random order
check.pseudocode: for src in gen(): f = Outline(ctx, abs, src, opts); assert f.Backend in {go/ast,ctags,heuristic,none}; assert f.Decls != nil; assert sorted(f.Decls, key=(StartLine,Name)) == f.Decls

criteria.action: for any Decl it returns, set Kind to one of func, method, type, class, interface, enum, trait, const, var, module or macro, and drop any declaration whose backend vocabulary does not map into that set (locals, parameters, fields, struct members, enumerators, labels, imports)
criteria.contract: every Decl.Kind is in {func, method, type, class, interface, enum, trait, const, var, module, macro}; no Decl is produced for locals, parameters, fields, struct members, enumerators, labels or imports

setup: Go sources with locals, struct fields, imports and labels
fake ctags output containing field, local, parameter, enumerator, label, import and unknown kinds
check.pseudocode: for input in gen(): for d in Outline(...).Decls: assert d.Kind in CLOSED_SET

criteria.action: keep only top-level declarations and methods of a declared type, with StartLine and EndLine 1-based and inclusive and EndLine 0 when the backend cannot tell
criteria.contract: the func and the method are present with StartLine and EndLine matching the source lines; no local var/type and no struct field appears; a backend that cannot tell end yields EndLine 0

setup: a Go file with a top-level func, a method, a func-local var and type, a struct field, on known lines
a ctags fake with a tag whose scope is a function (a local)
check.pseudocode: f = Outline(goFile); assert names(f.Decls) == ['Top','Method']; assert f.Decls[0].StartLine == 3 and EndLine == 5

criteria.action: for any source line, produce a Signature that contains no newline and no control character, has each run of whitespace collapsed to one space, and is at most 200 bytes long
criteria.contract: Signature contains no \n, \r or other control character; Signature contains no run of two or more whitespace characters; len(Signature) <= 200 and Signature is valid UTF-8

setup: a generator of source lines with newlines, tabs, runs of spaces, control characters and arbitrary lengths
check.pseudocode: for line in gen(): s = sig(line); assert no_ctrl(s); assert '  ' not in s; assert len(s) <= 200; assert utf8.valid(s)

criteria.condition: a signature exceeds 200 bytes and a multi-byte rune straddles byte 200
criteria.action: cut the signature before that rune so the result is valid UTF-8 and at most 200 bytes
criteria.contract: the returned Signature never ends in a partial rune

setup: a source line where a 3-byte rune occupies bytes 199-201 and another case with a 2-byte rune straddling byte 200
check.pseudocode: line = 'a'*198 + '世' + 'tail'; s = sig(line); assert utf8.valid(s) and len(s) == 198

criteria.condition: Options.Root is non-empty
criteria.action: set File.Path to the slash-separated path of the file relative to Root
criteria.contract: File.Path equals "sub/dir/a.go"; the path contains no backslash on any platform

setup: a temp root with sub/dir/a.go
check.pseudocode: f = Outline(ctx, root/sub/dir/a.go, nil, {Root: root}); assert f.Path == 'sub/dir/a.go'

criteria.condition: Options.Root is empty
criteria.action: set File.Path to the slash-converted absolute path rather than a relative one
criteria.contract: File.Path equals filepath.ToSlash(abs); File.Path is not relative

setup: a temp file a.go
check.pseudocode: f = Outline(ctx, abs, nil, {}); assert f.Path == ToSlash(abs)

requirements.title: Outline entry points and file eligibility
requirements.rationale: Callers need cheap rejection of files that cannot be outlined and a predictable error contract for single and batch calls.

criteria.condition: Source.Src is nil
criteria.action: read the file at Source.Abs itself before outlining it
criteria.contract: the nil-Src call returns declarations from the disk content; the Src call returns declarations from the supplied bytes

setup: a file on disk whose content differs from an in-memory Src
check.pseudocode: assert names(Outline(abs,nil).Decls) == ['OnDisk']; assert names(Outline(abs,[]byte(other)).Decls) == ['InMemory']

criteria.condition: the file extension is outside the fixed table (Go, Python, JS/TS, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, Ruby, C/C++ and the further ctags languages PHP, Swift, Scala, Lua, shell and Perl)
criteria.action: return File with Lang "" and Backend "none" and an empty non-nil Decls without reading the file
criteria.contract: no file read occurs for such an extension

setup: a path foo.xyz that does not exist on disk, and a table of in-table extensions (.go .py .js .ts .rs .java .kt .cs .rb .c .cpp .php .swift .scala .lua .sh .pl) for Lang detection
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(ctx, '/nonexistent/foo.xyz', nil, opts); assert err == nil; assert f.Lang == '' and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

criteria.condition: the file is larger than Options.MaxFileBytes, where zero means 1 MiB
criteria.action: return the File with Backend "none" and no declarations
criteria.contract: no error is returned; a file of exactly MaxFileBytes is still outlined

setup: a Go file of exactly MaxFileBytes bytes, one of MaxFileBytes+1 bytes, and one just over 1 MiB with MaxFileBytes 0
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(big, {MaxFileBytes: n}); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'none' and len(f.Decls) == 0

criteria.condition: the file contains a NUL byte within its first 8 KiB
criteria.action: return the File with Backend "none" and no declarations
criteria.contract: no error is returned

setup: a .py file with a NUL at offset 100, and one with a NUL only after offset 8192
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(nulFile); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

criteria.condition: the context is cancelled before or during Outline or OutlineMany
criteria.action: stop and return the context's error
criteria.contract: the returned error equals ctx.Err()

setup: a context cancelled before the call
a second context cancelled during a blocking fake Runner
check.pseudocode: cancel(); _, err = Outline(ctx, ...); assert err == ctx.Err(); _, _, err = OutlineMany(ctx, ...); assert err == ctx.Err()

criteria.condition: Outline cannot read the file
criteria.action: return a non-nil error
criteria.contract: Outline returns an error and the zero File

setup: a .py path that does not exist, or is a directory, with nil Src
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(ctx, missing, nil, opts); assert err != nil; assert f == File{}

criteria.condition: OutlineMany cannot read one of the files
criteria.action: return that file as Backend "none" with no declarations and continue with the remaining files
criteria.contract: OutlineMany returns a nil error for that file and every other file is outlined

setup: three Sources: a readable .go, a missing .py with nil Src, a readable .go
check.pseudocode: fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, {}); assert err == nil; assert fs[1].Backend == 'none'; assert len(fs[0].Decls) > 0

criteria.action: for any input slice of Sources, return from OutlineMany a []File with one entry per input in input order, together with a Stats value
criteria.contract: len(result) == len(input); result[i].Path corresponds to input[i].Abs for every i; a Stats value is returned

setup: a generator of Source slices mixing languages, unknown extensions, unreadable and oversize files
check.pseudocode: for srcs in gen(): fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, opts); assert len(fs) == len(srcs); for i: assert fs[i].Path == rel(srcs[i].Abs)

requirements.title: Go backend
requirements.rationale: Go declarations and ranges are available exactly from go/ast without any subprocess.

criteria.condition: the file has the .go extension
criteria.action: parse it with go/parser.ParseFile using parser.SkipObjectResolution, set Backend "go/ast" and spawn no subprocess
criteria.contract: Backend is go/ast and Lang is go; the Runner is not called

setup: a valid Go file
a Runner that fails the test when invoked
check.pseudocode: f = Outline(goFile, {Runner: failRunner}); assert f.Backend == 'go/ast'; assert runnerCalls == 0

criteria.condition: the file declares a function or a method
criteria.action: emit kind func for a function and kind method for a method, with Container set to the receiver's base type name without "*" and without type parameters
criteria.contract: F has kind func and empty Container; M and N have kind method with Container T; P has kind method with Container G (no * and no type parameters)

setup: Go source with func F(), func (t *T) M(), func (t T) N(), and func (g *G[K, V]) P()
check.pseudocode: assert d('P').Kind == 'method' and d('P').Container == 'G'

criteria.condition: the file declares type, const or var specs
criteria.action: emit kind interface for an interface type and kind type for every other type, and emit one const or var Decl per declared name while skipping the blank identifier "_"
criteria.contract: the interface has kind interface; struct, defined type and alias have kind type; A, B are two const Decls; x, y are two var Decls; no Decl is named _

setup: Go source with an interface type, a struct type, a defined type, an alias, const (A, B = 1, 2; _ = 3), and var x, y int
check.pseudocode: assert kinds == {'I':'interface','S':'type','A':'const','B':'const','x':'var','y':'var'}; assert '_' not in names

criteria.action: for any Go source, set StartLine and EndLine of each Decl equal to the go/ast node positions in the token.FileSet, starting at the keyword (or at the spec inside a grouped declaration) and excluding the doc comment
criteria.contract: each Decl StartLine/EndLine equals fset.Position of the node/spec Pos and End; a doc comment line is never StartLine; for a grouped declaration the range is that of the spec, not the keyword

setup: a corpus of generated and fixture Go sources with doc comments and grouped declarations
check.pseudocode: for src in gen(): f = Outline(src); want = reference(src); assert [(d.Name,d.StartLine,d.EndLine) for d in f.Decls] == want

criteria.action: for any Decl, set Exported equal to ast.IsExported(Name)
criteria.contract: every Decl has Exported == ast.IsExported(Name)

setup: generated Go identifiers including Unicode upper-case, lower-case and underscore-leading names
check.pseudocode: for d in Outline(src).Decls: assert d.Exported == ast.IsExported(d.Name)

criteria.action: write Signature as "func ..." up to the body for functions and methods, "type Name struct" or "type Name interface" for those types, "type Name <underlying type expression>" on one line for other types, and "const Name" or "var Name [Type]" for const and var
criteria.contract: func signature is "func ..." up to the body on one line, without the body; signatures are "type S struct", "type I interface", "type M map[string]int"; const is "const C", var is "var V int" and "var W" without a type

setup: Go source with a multi-line func signature with body, type S struct, type I interface, type M map[string]int, type A = []byte, const C, var V int, var W
check.pseudocode: assert sig('S') == 'type S struct'; assert sig('V') == 'var V int'

criteria.condition: the Go file has syntax errors and the parser returns a partial AST
criteria.action: use the partial AST for declarations and keep Backend "go/ast"
criteria.contract: declarations before and after the syntax error that the parser recovered are returned and no error is returned

setup: Go source with valid func A, a syntax error in the middle, then valid func B
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(broken); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'go/ast'; assert {'A','B'} <= names(f.Decls)

criteria.condition: the parser returns no AST at all
criteria.action: fall through to the next backend as for any other language
criteria.contract: no error is returned; the result is produced by ctags, heuristic or none

setup: the package's parse seam replaced by a stub returning a nil *ast.File
once with a fake Runner returning a valid tag for the .go file, once with a nil Runner
check.pseudocode: parseHook = func(...) { return nil, err }; f, err = Outline(goFile, {Runner: fake}); assert err == nil and f.Backend == 'ctags'

requirements.title: ctags invocation, batching and parsing
requirements.rationale: ctags output is untrusted external data, so the argument list is fixed and every line is validated before it is attributed to a file.

criteria.condition: a non-Go file in the extension table is outlined and Options.Runner is non-nil
criteria.action: call the Runner with the arguments --options=NONE first, then --output-format=json, --fields=+neKS, --sort=no, -f, -, followed by the explicit absolute file paths and without the program name
criteria.contract: args[0] is "--options=NONE"; args[1:6] are "--output-format=json", "--fields=+neKS", "--sort=no", "-f", "-"; the remaining args are the absolute file paths; args do not include the program name "ctags"

setup: a recording fake Runner returning empty output
a .py file with an absolute path
check.pseudocode: assert args[:6] == ['--options=NONE','--output-format=json','--fields=+neKS','--sort=no','-f','-'][:6] ; assert args[6:] == [abs]

criteria.action: never pass a directory or -R to the Runner, pass absolute paths only so that no file name begins with "-", and never spawn a process itself
criteria.contract: no argument equals -R and no argument after position 5 is a directory; every file argument is absolute and starts with the path separator or drive letter, never '-'; the recorded Runner is the only external call (no os/exec use in the package)

setup: Sources whose names begin with '-' in a relative-looking directory, and a directory path passed as a Source
PATH set to empty so any spawn attempt would fail
a recording Runner
check.pseudocode: for a in args[6:]: assert filepath.IsAbs(a) and not a.startswith('-'); assert '-R' not in args

criteria.action: for any call to OutlineMany, group files into batches of at most 100 files and at most 32 KiB of path text and make one Runner call per batch rather than one per file
criteria.contract: every Runner call has at most 100 file args; the summed byte length of path args per call is at most 32 KiB; the number of calls is far fewer than the number of files (e.g. 101 short files give exactly 2 calls); every file appears in exactly one call

setup: a recording fake Runner
a generator of file counts (0..350) and path lengths (1..4000 bytes)
check.pseudocode: for files in gen(): OutlineMany(files, fake); for c in calls: assert len(c.files)<=100 and sum(map(len,c.files))<=32768; assert union(calls)==files

criteria.condition: Options.Runner is nil
criteria.action: skip the ctags backend and handle each file with the heuristic backend or none
criteria.contract: the Python file has Backend heuristic; the Lua file has Backend none; Stats reports no fallback (ctags was never attempted)

setup: a .py file, a .lua file and Options{Runner: nil}
check.pseudocode: fs, st, _ = OutlineMany(srcs, {}); assert fs[0].Backend == 'heuristic' and fs[1].Backend == 'none'; assert st.Fallbacks == 0

criteria.condition: an output line has a _type other than "tag"
criteria.action: ignore the line without counting it as malformed
criteria.contract: only the valid tag becomes a Decl; Stats malformed count is 0

setup: fake output with a ptag line (_type: ptag), a !_TAG_ line, and one valid tag line
check.pseudocode: assert len(f.Decls) == 1; assert st.MalformedLines == 0

criteria.condition: an output line is not valid JSON or lacks a name, path or line
criteria.action: skip the line and increment the malformed-line count in Stats
criteria.contract: the line yields no Decl and no error is returned

setup: fake output with: truncated JSON, a tag without name, a tag without path, a tag without line, and one valid tag
check.pseudocode: assert err == nil and st.MalformedLines == 4 and len(f.Decls) == 1

criteria.condition: a tag echoes a path that was not in the batch
criteria.action: drop the tag
criteria.contract: no File in the result contains a Decl from that tag

setup: a batch of a.py and a fake output tag with path /elsewhere/z.py plus a valid tag for a.py
check.pseudocode: for f in fs: assert 'Foreign' not in names(f.Decls)

criteria.condition: a valid tag line is read
criteria.action: attribute the tag to the file whose path the tag echoes, not to the file at the same position in the batch
criteria.contract: a.py has only its own Decl and b.py only its own; the untagged file has empty Decls and Backend ctags

setup: a batch [a.py, b.py] and fake output listing b.py's tag before a.py's tag, and a file with no tags
check.pseudocode: assert names(fs[0].Decls) == ['inA'] and names(fs[1].Decls) == ['inB']

requirements.title: ctags result mapping and fallback
requirements.rationale: ctags is optional at run time, so a broken installation must degrade to the heuristic backend and not fail the outline.

criteria.action: normalise each ctags kind into the closed Kind set, map struct-like kinds to type, and drop tags whose kind does not map
criteria.contract: function→func, class→class, struct→type, interface→interface, enum→enum, trait→trait, variable→var, constant→const, module→module, macro→macro; member, field, local, enumerator, label, import and parameter produce no Decl

setup: fake tags with kinds function, class, struct, interface, enum, trait, variable, constant, module, macro, member, field, local, enumerator, label, import, parameter
check.pseudocode: assert kinds(f.Decls) == expected_mapped; assert dropped_names not in names

criteria.condition: a function-kind tag has a scope kind of class, struct, interface, enum, trait or impl
criteria.action: emit kind method with Container set to the tag's scope
criteria.contract: the type-scoped tags have kind method and Container equal to their scope; the function-scoped tag is not reported as a method (dropped as local)

setup: fake function tags with scopeKind class, struct, interface, enum, trait, impl, and one with scopeKind function
check.pseudocode: assert d.Kind == 'method' and d.Container == 'Foo'

criteria.action: set EndLine from the ctags end field when present and to 0 otherwise
criteria.contract: the first Decl has EndLine 12; the second has EndLine 0

setup: one tag with end: 12 and one without an end field
check.pseudocode: assert d1.EndLine == 12 and d2.EndLine == 0

criteria.action: set Signature to the trimmed source line at StartLine and use the ctags signature field only when that line is unavailable
criteria.contract: the first Signature is "def foo(a, b):" (trimmed source line); the second Signature uses the ctags signature field

setup: a Src with '    def foo(a, b):  ' at line 3 and a tag with signature '(x)'
a tag whose line is beyond the end of the source
check.pseudocode: assert d1.Signature == 'def foo(a, b):'; assert d2.Signature == '(x)'

criteria.action: for any ctags Decl, set Exported to true unless the name begins with an underscore, and set the File's Backend to "ctags"
criteria.contract: Public is Exported true; _private and __dunder__ Exported false; File.Backend is ctags

setup: fake tags named Public, _private and __dunder__
check.pseudocode: assert exported == {'Public':True,'_private':False}; assert f.Backend == 'ctags'

criteria.condition: the Runner returns an error or a batch's output is not usable
criteria.action: handle every file in that batch with the heuristic backend when its language has one and otherwise return it as "none", and record the fallback in Stats
criteria.contract: OutlineMany returns a nil error for that batch and each affected File names its actual Backend

setup: a batch of a Python file and a Lua file
a Runner returning an error in one case and returning non-JSON garbage in another
check.pseudocode: fs, st, err = OutlineMany(srcs, {Runner: errRunner}); assert err == nil; assert [f.Backend for f in fs] == ['heuristic','none']; assert st.Fallbacks == 1

criteria.condition: the context is cancelled while the Runner is running
criteria.action: return the context's error and not fall back to the heuristic backend
criteria.contract: the returned error equals ctx.Err()

setup: a Runner that blocks until ctx is cancelled and returns ctx.Err()
a Python file
check.pseudocode: go cancelAfter(10ms); fs, st, err = OutlineMany(ctx, srcs, {Runner: blocking}); assert err == ctx.Err(); assert st.Fallbacks == 0

requirements.title: Heuristic and none backends
requirements.rationale: Ten common languages still get top-level declarations when ctags is absent, and everything else degrades visibly to none.

criteria.condition: a Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, Ruby, C or C++ file is handled without usable ctags
criteria.action: apply anchored line regular expressions to declarations starting at column 0, optionally after a modifier such as export, export default, async, pub, pub(crate), public or static, and set Backend "heuristic"
criteria.contract: Backend is heuristic for each; Decls equal the golden JSON; every Decl has Container "" and EndLine 0

setup: fixtures under outline/testdata for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Java, Kotlin, C#, Ruby, C and C++ with column-0 declarations after modifiers (export, export default, async, pub, pub(crate), public, static)
check.pseudocode: for lang in TEN: f = Outline(fixture(lang)); assert json(f) == golden(lang); for d in f.Decls: assert d.Container=='' and d.EndLine==0

criteria.action: set Container to empty and EndLine to 0 on every Decl

set Exported false for a leading underscore in Python and Ruby, for a missing pub in Rust, for a missing export in JavaScript and TypeScript and for a missing public in Java, Kotlin and C#, and set Exported true for C and C++
criteria.contract: underscore names are not exported in Python and Ruby; Rust without pub, JS/TS without export, Java/Kotlin/C# without public are not exported; with them they are exported; C and C++ Decls are all exported

setup: fixtures with: Python/Ruby _name vs name; Rust fn vs pub fn; JS/TS function vs export function; Java/Kotlin/C# without vs with public; C and C++ functions
check.pseudocode: assert exported('rust','fn a')==False and exported('rust','pub fn a')==True

criteria.condition: a declaration is indented, such as a method inside a class
criteria.action: not report it
criteria.contract: the Decls list contains no indented declaration

setup: a Python file with class A: and an indented '    def m(self):', and a JS class with an indented method
check.pseudocode: assert names(f.Decls) == ['A']

criteria.condition: the language has no heuristic and ctags is unavailable or unusable
criteria.action: return the File with Backend "none", the detected Lang and an empty non-nil Decls
criteria.contract: no error is returned and the file remains in any walk that listed it

setup: a .lua file, with a nil Runner and with a failing Runner
check.pseudocode: f, err = Outline(lua, {}); assert err == nil and f.Lang == 'lua' and f.Backend == 'none' and f.Decls == []

requirements.title: tools.CtagsRunner
requirements.rationale: The process lifecycle (reduced environment, deadline, process-group kill, bounded output) lives in tools so outline needs no first-party import.

criteria.condition: CtagsRunner(env) is called
criteria.action: return a func(ctx context.Context, args []string) ([]byte, error) that is assignable to outline.Options.Runner
criteria.contract: tools does not import outline

setup: a tools_test or external test file importing both packages
check.pseudocode: var _ = outline.Options{Runner: tools.CtagsRunner(nil)}; assert 'outline' not in goList('./tools').Imports

criteria.action: locate ctags with exec.LookPath once per runner and confirm it is universal-ctags by running `ctags --version` and finding "Universal Ctags" in the output
criteria.contract: Exuberant and BSD variants return errors wrapping ErrCtagsUnavailable on every call; the Universal variant runs the requested arguments successfully; --version is executed exactly once per runner

setup: a fake 'ctags' shell script on PATH that appends to a counter file on each --version call (skipped on windows)
variants printing 'Exuberant Ctags 5.8', a BSD usage error, and 'Universal Ctags 6.0'
check.pseudocode: assert errors.Is(err, ErrCtagsUnavailable) for non-universal; assert count(versionCalls) == 1

criteria.condition: ctags is absent from PATH or its version output lacks "Universal Ctags"
criteria.action: return an error wrapping the exported sentinel ErrCtagsUnavailable on every call without spawning any further process
criteria.contract: errors.Is(err, ErrCtagsUnavailable) is true

setup: PATH set to an empty directory
check.pseudocode: t.Setenv('PATH', emptyDir); r = CtagsRunner(nil); _, e = r(ctx, args); assert errors.Is(e, ErrCtagsUnavailable)

criteria.action: run ctags with environment env, or ReducedEnv(nil) when env is nil
criteria.contract: with nil the child environment equals ReducedEnv(nil) and omits the secret variable; with env given the child sees exactly FOO=bar; stdin read yields EOF immediately; the stderr marker is absent from the returned stdout

setup: a fake universal ctags script that prints its environment and a stdin read to stdout and writes a marker to stderr
a secret variable in the test process environment
check.pseudocode: out = r(ctx, args); assert 'SECRET' not in out; assert 'STDERR_MARK' not in out

criteria.action: give the process an empty stdin, discard stderr, and capture stdout separately from stderr into an Accumulator in TruncateHead mode with a 16 MiB cap

criteria.condition: the Accumulator reports truncation
criteria.action: return an error instead of the cut-off stream
criteria.contract: the returned byte slice is not a partial stream and the error is non-nil

setup: the accumulator cap lowered through a test seam to 1 KiB
a fake or real ctags that emits more than 1 KiB on stdout
check.pseudocode: out, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil and out == nil

criteria.condition: the context ends while ctags is running
criteria.action: kill the whole process group with killGroup, as execute does
criteria.contract: no ctags process of that call remains running after the call returns

setup: a fake universal ctags script that spawns a background child sleep and then sleeps itself (skipped on windows)
where real ctags is present the same check is run against it
check.pseudocode: go cancelAfter(100ms); _, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil; assert not alive(pid) and not alive(childPid)

criteria.condition: ctags exits with a non-zero status
criteria.action: return an error
criteria.contract: the error is non-nil and the call returns no usable stdout

setup: a fake universal ctags script that prints some output and exits 3 when not called with --version
check.pseudocode: out, err = r(ctx, args); assert err != nil and out == nil

requirements.title: One directory walk and tools.Walk
requirements.rationale: One traversal guarantees that every consumer of workspace files sees the same set of files the file tools see.

criteria.action: build newIgnoreEngine(root, opts), compute for each entry other than the root its slash-separated path relative to the root, skip (SkipDir for a directory) any entry the ignore engine matches and any dot-prefixed entry when hidden entries are excluded, call the callback for files and directories, and call ig.enter for each directory the callback did not skip
criteria.contract: rel is slash-separated and never includes the root entry; ignored entries (including those from the nested .gitignore, applied only after ig.enter on their directory) are not called back; an ignored directory is not descended; dot-prefixed entries are absent when hidden is excluded and present when included (except those the ignore engine matches such as .git); directories are called back as well as files

setup: a temp tree with a root .gitignore, a nested dir with its own .gitignore, .git, a .hidden file and dir, ignored entries and regular files
check.pseudocode: walk(ctx, root, IgnoreOptions{}, false, rec); assert rels == expectedNoHidden; walk(..., true, rec); assert '.hidden' in rels and '.git' not in rels

criteria.condition: an entry is unreadable or the root does not exist
criteria.action: skip the unreadable entry without error, and make no callback calls for a missing root
criteria.contract: the walk returns a nil error in both cases

setup: a root path that does not exist
a tree with a directory whose permissions are 000 (skipped on windows or when running as root)
check.pseudocode: err = walk(ctx, missing, ...); assert err == nil and calls == 0

criteria.condition: the context is cancelled
criteria.action: check the context for each entry and stop the walk
criteria.contract: the walk returns ctx.Err()

setup: a tree with several files
a context cancelled from inside the callback after the first entry, and another cancelled before the walk
